pathway.title: Encompass Health Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Payment policy and claim review, not demand, are the dominant credit risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 lifts Medicare rates by only 2.3% from 2026-10-01, below the 3.5% to 4.0% rise the company guides for salaries and benefits per employee, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on its largest payer. Claim review compounds this: coverage rises from about 11.9% of Medicare claims to about 63% on 2027-01-01, 5.29x as many, and in Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the validation rate needed to opt out of full pre-claim review in the second or third cycle. Bad-debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 revenue against 1.9% a year earlier, and receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in nine months against USD 18.8 million. Delay and denial therefore reach cash flow before they reach reported demand. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30, 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C4; calculation C11; calculation C27

Earnings growth, not debt repayment, is what lowers leverage, and the pace is set to slow. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 to USD 346.6 million, and the nine-month margin was 21.77% against 21.23% because the extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58%. Total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.96x at 2025-12-31 and 1.88x at 2026-09-30, since last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 8.76% above FY2025 while debt is 4.35% higher. Guidance of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million for 2026 implies Q4 growth of only 4.77% to 10.73%, so further deleveraging needs earnings growth or repayment that management has not committed to. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

Liquidity and maturity timing give creditors a long runway, but the bond wall is concentrated. Liquidity was USD 947.6 million at 2026-09-30, and the undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million, which runs to 2031-03-09, covers the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value, and the 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced. Net debt was USD 2,522.9 million, or USD 2,543.8 million pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-15 at its declared amount of USD 20.9 million, which is 1.62x reported EBITDA or 1.64x pro forma. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 18, 20, 40; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C16

Capital allocation is the controllable risk and it is moving the wrong way. Operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capital spending of USD 617.2 million and partner distributions of USD 141.8 million left USD 198.7 million, against dividends and repurchases of USD 261.6 million. On the issuer's own measure, which starts from Adjusted EBITDA and deducts cash interest, cash taxes and maintenance capital spending, the nine months left USD 634.2 million, and after growth capital of USD 451.2 million and shareholder returns the result was a shortfall of USD 78.6 million against a surplus of USD 82.1 million a year earlier. The two measures differ in perimeter but agree in direction. About USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remained at 2026-09-30, 4.69x the nine-month repurchases of USD 203.7 million, and management gives no debt-reduction assumption for 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C25

Cash conversion is good but slipping as taxes and growth capital rise. Issuer-defined free cash flow was 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA in nine months against 62.48% a year earlier and 64.51% in FY2025, and the 2026 guidance of USD 770 million to USD 865 million implies 55.20% to 61.13% of guided Adjusted EBITDA. Cash tax payments were USD 87.3 million higher than in the nine months of 2025, equal to 78.58% of the USD 111.1 million gain in Adjusted EBITDA and partly tax paid in 2026 for an underpayment in 2025, and maintenance capital spending rose USD 25.5 million. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending, which management can slow, but about USD 535 million is still to be spent on projects already under construction. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C18

Interest cover is comfortable on every basis available. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 10.55x in FY2025 and income-statement interest 12.23x over the last twelve months. On guided cash interest of USD 115 million to USD 125 million and guided Adjusted EBITDA, cover would be 11.16x to 12.30x, although the issuer's cash interest measure ran USD 19.5 million below the cash paid in the annual report for 2025, so the cash-basis ratio could be lower. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17

Referral and partner dependence concentrate operating risk that the filings do not size. About 92% of patients come from acute-care hospitals, which also run competing rehabilitation units, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures whose partners received USD 141.8 million in nine months, 14.81% of operating cash flow, and hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million. A partner's distress or exit would hit volume and could call cash, in an amount that is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

The sector structure supports pricing, but its protective barriers are thinning at the edges. The industry outside the company is highly fragmented, patients aged 75 and over are expected to grow about 4% a year through 2030, and about 36% of licensed beds sit in states with certificate-of-need laws, but North Carolina repealed its certificate-of-need requirement for certain providers in July 2026. The annual Medicare update fell from 2.6% for fiscal 2026 to 2.3% for fiscal 2027, and a reform that paid all post-acute care under one system would, on an advisory-body estimate the company cannot verify, cut inpatient rehabilitation payments by 15%. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 29, 34, 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 37; calculation C22

Covenant and legal protection cannot be established, so none is relied on here. The credit agreement sets a maximum leverage ratio of 4.50x and a minimum interest coverage of 3.0x and the company states compliance, but the ratios achieved, the adjustments in their definitions and the executed agreements are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; Financial foundation (CP-1)

cells.text: Largest owner and operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals by patients treated, revenues and hospitals, in the company's own words; one reportable segment
177 hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico
One service line and one payer system, so there is no segment diversification to offset a rate or review shock
Per-discharge payment: inpatient revenue is discharges times net patient revenue per discharge
FY2025: discharges 263,299; net patient revenue per discharge USD 21,862; inpatient revenue USD 5,756.3 million
Volume and price are the two levers; price per discharge rose 3.87% and volume 5.96%
Medicare and Medicare Advantage dominate; rates are set by federal rule
Medicare 65.7%; Medicare Advantage 16.1%; managed care 10.7%; Medicaid 3.0%
Revenue is exposed to annual rate-setting and to claim-review rules rather than to negotiated contracts
Substantially all patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals after physician referral
Referral relationships, including joint-venture partners, drive volume and are not quantified by source
New hospitals and bed additions; discharge growth is split between same-store and new capacity
New capacity 2.9 percentage points of 5.2% total discharge growth
Roughly half of volume growth needs new capital before it earns
Occupancy leaves room to fill existing beds, which is a cheaper source of growth than new hospitals
Labour is the largest cost; contract labour fell while internal staff grew
Salaries and benefits 51.72% of revenue; employees per occupied bed 3.34; contract labour FTEs 317 against 370
Labour inflation and staffing shortages are the main margin risk; the reported improvement is recent
The company owns the building at most hospitals
Building owned at 137 of 173 hospitals, 79.19%; about 8% of hospitals leased per the contractual obligations note
Owned real estate is a source of secured-debt capacity and recovery value that the filings do not value
Hospitals held with health-system partners that hold noncontrolling interests and, in some cases, put rights
About 38% of hospitals; noncontrolling interests USD 821.4 million plus USD 58.6 million redeemable
Partners share profits and distributions and fund some growth; partner exits could call cash
Discretionary growth capital on top of maintenance capital
2026 plan USD 920 million to USD 995 million; maintenance USD 225 million to USD 240 million; about USD 535 million more to complete projects under construction
The discretionary share is a lever, but cash flow is committed to it in good years

runs.text: The first strength is earnings growth that lowers leverage without repayment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 and total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.88x at 2026-09-30, because extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58% against an average margin of 21.23%; this widens the gap between cash flow and debt service and supports a low probability of distress while volumes keep growing. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

The second strength is a long liquidity and maturity runway. Liquidity of USD 947.6 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million to 2031 cover the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x, so refinancing risk is remote until 2028 and any slower earnings would be absorbed before creditors are affected. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 40; calculation C2; calculation C16

The third strength is non-discretionary, rule-priced demand that is still growing. Discharges rose 5.7% in Q3 and the Medicare rate update of 2.3% from 2026-10-01 sets price in advance, with an ageing population adding about 4% a year to the 75-and-over group, which gives revenue visibility that supports debt service through a normal cycle. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14

The fourth strength is discretionary growth spending. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending and the 2026 growth plan of USD 695 million to USD 755 million is more than six times the USD 111.1 million fall in earnings used in the downside, so management can protect liquidity in a downturn by slowing expansion. Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

The fifth strength is owned real estate against an unsecured bond structure. The company owns the building at 79.19% of its hospitals and only the revolver is stated to be secured, so a large asset base sits outside the secured claim, although its value and the recovery it would support are not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The first weakness is payer concentration under widening review. Medicare and Medicare Advantage paid 81.8% of revenue and review will cover about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, up from about 11.9%, so a delay or denial pushes cash collection back before any change in demand, a mechanism already visible in a bad-debt reserve of 2.7% of Q3 revenue and in Alabama, where no hospital reached the opt-out rate in two cycles. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; calculation C4; calculation C15; calculation C27

The second weakness is capital allocation that outruns cash flow. Shareholder returns exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million while debt rose USD 108.3 million, and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains, so leverage can stop falling by choice and debt holders carry that policy risk. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C25

The third weakness is labour cost that is outrunning the Medicare price. Salaries and benefits are 51.72% of revenue and guided to rise 3.5% to 4.0% per employee against a 2.3% Medicare update, so margins depend on staffing productivity that has to keep improving to hold the 21.77% nine-month margin. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 30; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C20

The fourth weakness is a concentrated bond wall at a higher cost. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value and new 2034 debt carries a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes, so refinancing depends on market access in those years and will probably cost more interest. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; calculation C2; calculation C16

The fifth weakness is dependence on referral sources and joint-venture partners. About 92% of patients are referred by acute-care hospitals that also run competing units, and partners took USD 141.8 million of distributions in nine months while holding put rights on terms that are not disclosed, so volume and cash calls can change without any change in policy. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

cells.text: Encompass Health Corporation, a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1984; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in USD millions
Common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under EHC; large accelerated filer and well-known seasoned issuer
Inpatient rehabilitation hospitals providing specialized rehabilitative treatment; sector in the run settings is Services-Hospitals
177 at 2026-09-30, of which 110 are sole-owned and 67 are joint ventures with 50.0% to 97.5% company ownership; 173 at 2025-12-31 and 166 at 2024-12-31
39 states and Puerto Rico; Texas 29 and Florida 25 hospitals at 2025-12-31
Over 42,000 employees at 2025-12-31 and about 44,000 at 2026-09-30; none represented by a union except 50 employees at one hospital
One reportable segment; net operating revenues USD 5,935.2 million in FY2025 and USD 4,793.5 million in nine months 2026
Public company; no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified; 98,123,613 shares outstanding at 2026-10-22; beneficial ownership table not supplied
About USD 12.2 billion at 2025-06-30; directors and executive officers deemed affiliates

Ten directors signed the annual report, including a chair who is separate from the President and Chief Executive Officer; an Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer and a Chief Accounting Officer also signed; independence and committees are in the proxy statement
PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, auditor since 2003, with an opinion on internal control over financial reporting

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No sponsor transaction, buyout, merger or acquisition is described in the sources, and none is pending; the 2026 activity is refinancing and a small disposal. On March 9, 2026 the company entered a new credit agreement with Truist Bank as agent that replaced the 2022 agreement, moved the revolver maturity to March 2031, lowered the fee on undrawn commitments by 5 bp, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, and raised the swingline sublimit from USD 25 million to USD 40 million. It drew USD 250.0 million on the revolver that month to retire the old facility. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ehc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.2_2026-04-30_ehcq12026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5

In May 2026 the company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034 at par, raising about USD 491 million net, and used the proceeds with cash to redeem USD 400 million of the USD 800 million 2028 notes at par and repay USD 100 million of the revolver, recording a USD 3.2 million loss on early extinguishment. In August 2026 it sold a further USD 100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% of principal, raising about USD 97 million net, to repay part of the revolver. The 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced, so the refinancing extended maturities at a higher running cost. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ehc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.2_2026-08-05_ehcq22026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C15; calculation C16

The only disposal is the sale of the 50% interest in the Gamma Knife Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital to the joint-venture partner for USD 17.9 million, agreed on 2025-12-31 and effective on 2026-01-01, which produced a USD 17.5 million pre-tax gain in other income. In July 2024 the company contributed a wholly owned 70-bed Augusta hospital to its Piedmont joint venture, and Piedmont paid about USD 90 million for a 50% interest in it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 167, 187

fields.value: Encompass Health Corp (issuer id ehc), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: financial foundation for the consolidated Encompass Health Corporation group, covering FY2024, FY2025, nine months and the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, debt, liquidity, constructed last-twelve-month figures and leverage at 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, peers, deal terms or portfolio limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health's leverage is low and still falling, but only because earnings are growing: debt has not fallen and 2026 shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow after joint-venture distributions, so creditor protection rests on management's capital allocation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At 2026-09-30 total debt was USD 2,599.1 million: 1.67x trailing reported EBITDA and 1.88x the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, which deducts joint-venture partners' income. Liquidity was USD 947.6 million, and no significant debt falls due before 2028. Interest cover is 10.55x on cash interest paid for FY2025, but cash interest for the last twelve months and the covenant ratios achieved are not printed, so cover at the latest date and covenant headroom are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell on earnings growth, not repayment. Total debt was USD 2,497.8 million at 2024-12-31, USD 2,490.8 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 2,599.1 million at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,186.6 million in FY2024 to USD 1,404.1 million in FY2025 and USD 1,552.6 million over the last twelve months. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore moved from 2.11x to 1.77x to 1.67x, and net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.03x to 1.72x to 1.62x. Debt rose by USD 108.3 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, the period in which the company replaced its revolving facility, used new 2034 notes to redeem half of the 2028 notes and sold a further USD 100.0 million of the 2034 notes in August 2026 to repay part of the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's own earnings measure is the more conservative guide to cash that reaches the parent. The issuer states only an Adjusted EBITDA, which deducts the income of noncontrolling interests, USD 160.9 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and adds back share-based compensation. Reported EBITDA, calculated here from pre-tax income, interest and depreciation, is USD 134.9 million higher than the issuer's measure for that period. On the issuer's measure total debt is 2.26x, 1.96x and 1.88x Adjusted EBITDA at the three dates, in line with the issuer's own rounded 2.0x at 2025-12-31 and 1.9x at 2026-09-30. Joint-venture partners received USD 141.8 million of distributions in the nine months, so the deduction is a cash cost and not an accounting convention.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong but is largely absorbed by growth spending and distributions. In FY2025 net cash from operating activities of USD 1,175.6 million funded USD 736.4 million of capital spending and USD 152.1 million of joint-venture distributions, leaving USD 287.1 million; dividends and repurchases took USD 229.1 million of that and left USD 58.0 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 the same sequence left USD 198.7 million before dividends of USD 57.9 million and repurchases of USD 203.7 million, a shortfall of USD 62.9 million in a period when total debt rose by USD 108.3 million. Growth capital spending was USD 451.2 million in those nine months and capital spending ran at 12.88% of net operating revenues, so the pace at which leverage keeps falling is mainly a management choice.

fields.value: Interest cover is comfortable but cannot be carried to the latest date on a cash basis. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 8.08x in FY2024 and 10.55x in FY2025. Cash interest paid exceeded interest expense by USD 9.9 million in FY2025, and the company also capitalised USD 17.6 million of interest, and the annual report does not reconcile the cash paid with the expense. The quarterly reports do not print cash interest paid, so cover for the last twelve months is not calculable on that basis; against income-statement interest expense it is 12.23x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample and refinancing risk is remote before 2028. At 2026-09-30 cash of USD 76.2 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 871.4 million, after USD 75.0 million drawn and USD 53.6 million of letters of credit, gave liquidity of USD 947.6 million, or 0.36x total debt. The revolver matures on 2031-03-09, so no facility expires within twelve months, and scheduled principal through 2027 is only USD 56.2 million. The maturity wall then builds from USD 436.0 million in 2028 to USD 850.8 million in 2030, which is 32.35% of scheduled principal, and USD 515.1 million in 2031. Restricted cash of USD 24.0 million and restricted marketable securities of USD 158.5 million, held mainly for the captive insurer and joint-venture obligations, are excluded from liquidity.

Only the revolver is stated to be secured, so debt through the senior notes is 1.45x reported EBITDA; the finance leases and other notes are not ranked in the filings and sit outside that stack. Operating lease liabilities of USD 204.3 million and purchase obligations of USD 197.4 million sit outside the debt figure, and no pension, derivative, factoring or consent-decree obligation was found in any source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a benign reading is that growth and returns are being financed at the margin by debt. Capital spending of USD 617.2 million in nine months compares with a 2026 plan of USD 920 million to USD 995 million and about USD 535 million still to spend on projects under construction, and the board raised the repurchase authorization in July 2026. Receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in the nine months against USD 18.8 million a year earlier, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, which the issuer attributes to a billing and collecting disruption after a system conversion. If operating cash flow does not cover the remaining planned spending, or repurchases continue above free cash flow, leverage on the issuer's measure would stop falling. The view would improve if debt were repaid from free cash flow while EBITDA keeps growing, and weaken if trailing EBITDA fell, if the revolver were drawn to fund distributions, or if the covenant ratios, once supplied, showed less headroom than the compliance statements imply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health Corp (issuer id ehc), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: business, transaction, ownership, operating model and governance facts for the listed Encompass Health Corporation group, with no sponsor, ratings, market or portfolio inputs supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health is a scaled, government-paid inpatient rehabilitation operator with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so creditors face payment-policy and capital-allocation risk rather than ownership-extraction risk, though governance visibility is only moderate on the filings supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and 92% of patients are referred from acute-care hospitals, so a payment-rule or referral shock would reach revenue directly. Growth depends on opening new capacity, and shareholder returns of USD 261.6 million in those nine months exceeded the cash left after capital spending and joint-venture distributions. We rate sponsor and governance risk Medium because disclosed behaviour is mixed and the proxy statement and executed debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 33, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 165; calculation C1; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payment policy, not demand, is the main business risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of net operating revenues in the nine months to 2026-09-30, with Medicare alone at 65.7% for the nine months and 66.3% in the third quarter. Rates are reset each year by the federal payer, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 adds a net 2.3% to Medicare payment rates from October 2026, which supports pricing. The same payer is widening claim review: a demonstration that puts claims through pre-claim or post-payment review reached Texas in March 2026 and California in May 2026, and from January 2027 will cover about 63% of the company's Medicare claims. Denied claims of USD 39.0 million were under review at 2025-12-31, and revenue reserves for bad debt rose to 2.7% of revenue in the third quarter from 1.9%, so slower or lower collection is where a payment-policy shock would first reach cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Referral and partner relationships concentrate operating risk in counterparties the filings do not quantify. About 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures with health systems that also refer patients. Partners hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million, can require the company to buy certain interests at fair value, and received USD 141.8 million of distributions in the nine months to 2026-09-30. The company lists partner operating or financial strain as a risk, so a partner problem would be both a volume risk and a possible cash call.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12, 19; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is capital-hungry, so cash flow is committed to expansion before it is available for debt reduction. The network added 16 hospitals between the end of 2023 and 2026-09-30, and new capacity contributed 2.9 percentage points of the 5.2% discharge growth in the nine months, which is more than half of it. The 2026 capital plan is USD 920 million to USD 995 million, of which USD 225 million to USD 240 million is maintenance, with about USD 535 million more to finish projects now under construction. The non-maintenance part is discretionary, which gives management a lever in a downturn, but it also means leverage falls only if growth spending slows or earnings keep outrunning it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 36, 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11; calculation C9; calculation C7; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor, fund or controlling holder is identified, so sponsor-exit and fee-extraction risks are absent from the record, but the concentration of ownership is not established. The shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, non-affiliate market value was about USD 12.2 billion at 2025-06-30, the board chair is a director separate from the chief executive, related-party transactions were not material in 2025, 2024 or 2023, and the share count fell 1.30% between 2026-02-12 and 2026-10-22. The beneficial-ownership table sits in the 2026 proxy statement, which was not supplied, so a large holder with influence over distributions cannot be excluded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the creditor-relevant behaviour to watch, and they are rising while evidence of the legal room for them is not supplied. The quarterly dividend rose from USD 0.17 to USD 0.19 per share in July 2025 and to USD 0.21 in July 2026, repurchases rose from USD 31.1 million in FY2024 to USD 158.0 million in FY2025 and USD 203.7 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the board raised the repurchase authorization to USD 1.0 billion in July 2026. Dividends and repurchases took 19.49% of operating cash flow in FY2025 and 27.32% in the nine months, and in the nine months they exceeded the USD 198.7 million left after capital spending and joint-venture distributions by USD 62.9 million. The March 2026 credit agreement also relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, which widens the room for such returns, while no related-party fee, sponsor payment or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 136, 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 43, 44; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring but not yet a full governance read. The statements are audited by the same firm since 2003 with an opinion on internal control, the auditor named the valuation of patient receivables, including denied claims, as a critical audit matter, and the quarterly reports and slides reconcile the adjusted measures. Covenant compliance is stated without the ratios achieved, and directors' independence, compensation and beneficial ownership are in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the Medium rating reflects the limits of the evidence as well as the behaviour observed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading Medium as benign is that shareholder returns have begun to exceed the cash left after growth spending and partner distributions, in the same year lender restrictions were loosened and the repurchase authorization was raised to USD 1.0 billion. If the executed documents show wide restricted-payment capacity, that pattern would be a deliberate policy of leaning on the revolver and bond market, and the view would move to higher risk, although the arithmetic is thin, because the shortfall of USD 62.9 million compares with operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million. The view would move to Low if the proxy statement shows independent oversight and dispersed ownership, returns fall back below free cash flow and leverage keeps falling. A partner asking the company to buy its interest, or claim review delaying collections beyond the bad-debt reserve already taken, would also change the view because either reaches cash flow without any change in policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 44; calculation C11; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Board independence, committee structure, compensation design and beneficial ownership are not established because the 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so the Medium governance rating could move either way once it is read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens rests on the company's own summaries, which limits how firmly distributions can be called a policy choice rather than a constraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Geographic concentration in Florida and Texas is measured by hospital and bed counts, not revenue, so the concentration finding could be understated if those hospitals earn more than the average hospital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The effect of expanded claim review on collections cannot be quantified from the filings, so the payment-policy risk is stated as a direction and is not sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Growth targets, opening dates and guidance are management statements and tentative, so the conclusion that growth is funded from cash flow and the revolver describes a plan, not an outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Partner put-right terms and timing are disclosed only as a fair-value formula, so the size and timing of any cash call from a partner exit is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor transaction, buyout, merger or acquisition is described in the sources, and none is pending; the 2026 activity is refinancing and a small disposal. On March 9, 2026 the company entered a new credit agreement with Truist Bank as agent that replaced the 2022 agreement, moved the revolver maturity to March 2031, lowered the fee on undrawn commitments by 5 bp, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, and raised the swingline sublimit from USD 25 million to USD 40 million. It drew USD 250.0 million on the revolver that month to retire the old facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In May 2026 the company issued USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034 at par, raising about USD 491 million net, and used the proceeds with cash to redeem USD 400 million of the USD 800 million 2028 notes at par and repay USD 100 million of the revolver, recording a USD 3.2 million loss on early extinguishment. In August 2026 it sold a further USD 100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% of principal, raising about USD 97 million net, to repay part of the revolver. The 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced, so the refinancing extended maturities at a higher running cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ehc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.2_2026-08-05_ehcq22026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only disposal is the sale of the 50% interest in the Gamma Knife Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital to the joint-venture partner for USD 17.9 million, agreed on 2025-12-31 and effective on 2026-01-01, which produced a USD 17.5 million pre-tax gain in other income. In July 2024 the company contributed a wholly owned 70-bed Augusta hospital to its Piedmont joint venture, and Piedmont paid about USD 90 million for a 50% interest in it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. Evidence supports the business, transaction, ownership-structure and capital-allocation registers; the governance register is limited by the missing proxy statement and the sponsor registers do not apply because no sponsor is identified. Citation discipline: every fact carries a file and page; management statements are labelled as such.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Encompass Health presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is rising shareholder returns, with repurchases of USD 203.7 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and shareholder returns that exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million, which matters because it competes with debt reduction while the lender restrictions were loosened in March 2026, and implies a policy-driven rather than structural risk. Countervailing evidence is that earnings growth is lowering leverage, no sponsor, related-party leakage or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed, and the maturity profile was extended. Further analysis requires the 2026 proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indentures, and the covenant ratios achieved.
