fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health Corp (issuer id ehc), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: fundamental credit synthesis of the consolidated Encompass Health Corporation group from the seven supplied filings and presentations and the three earlier modules of this run. No ratings, market prices, peers, deal terms or portfolio limits were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health is a sound credit with low leverage whose main threat is Medicare payment policy and claim review, so creditors are protected today but depend on management keeping growth spending and repurchases within cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt of USD 2,599.1 million at 2026-09-30 was 1.88x the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, liquidity was USD 947.6 million and no significant debt matures before 2028. Medicare and Medicare Advantage paid 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and claim review will reach about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, up from about 11.9%. In the nine months, shareholder returns exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million while total debt rose USD 108.3 million, and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains. No rating is assigned, and covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 31, 33, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payment policy and claim review, not demand, are the dominant credit risk. Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 81.8% of nine-month revenue, and the final rule for fiscal 2027 lifts Medicare rates by only 2.3% from 2026-10-01, below the 3.5% to 4.0% rise the company guides for salaries and benefits per employee, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on its largest payer. Claim review compounds this: coverage rises from about 11.9% of Medicare claims to about 63% on 2027-01-01, 5.29x as many, and in Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the validation rate needed to opt out of full pre-claim review in the second or third cycle. Bad-debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 revenue against 1.9% a year earlier, and receivables absorbed USD 89.5 million of cash in nine months against USD 18.8 million. Delay and denial therefore reach cash flow before they reach reported demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30, 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C4; calculation C11; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings growth, not debt repayment, is what lowers leverage, and the pace is set to slow. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 to USD 346.6 million, and the nine-month margin was 21.77% against 21.23% because the extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58%. Total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.96x at 2025-12-31 and 1.88x at 2026-09-30, since last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 8.76% above FY2025 while debt is 4.35% higher. Guidance of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million for 2026 implies Q4 growth of only 4.77% to 10.73%, so further deleveraging needs earnings growth or repayment that management has not committed to.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturity timing give creditors a long runway, but the bond wall is concentrated. Liquidity was USD 947.6 million at 2026-09-30, and the undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million, which runs to 2031-03-09, covers the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value, and the 2034 notes carry a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes they partly replaced. Net debt was USD 2,522.9 million, or USD 2,543.8 million pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-15 at its declared amount of USD 20.9 million, which is 1.62x reported EBITDA or 1.64x pro forma.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 18, 20, 40; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is the controllable risk and it is moving the wrong way. Operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capital spending of USD 617.2 million and partner distributions of USD 141.8 million left USD 198.7 million, against dividends and repurchases of USD 261.6 million. On the issuer's own measure, which starts from Adjusted EBITDA and deducts cash interest, cash taxes and maintenance capital spending, the nine months left USD 634.2 million, and after growth capital of USD 451.2 million and shareholder returns the result was a shortfall of USD 78.6 million against a surplus of USD 82.1 million a year earlier. The two measures differ in perimeter but agree in direction. About USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remained at 2026-09-30, 4.69x the nine-month repurchases of USD 203.7 million, and management gives no debt-reduction assumption for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is good but slipping as taxes and growth capital rise. Issuer-defined free cash flow was 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA in nine months against 62.48% a year earlier and 64.51% in FY2025, and the 2026 guidance of USD 770 million to USD 865 million implies 55.20% to 61.13% of guided Adjusted EBITDA. Cash tax payments were USD 87.3 million higher than in the nine months of 2025, equal to 78.58% of the USD 111.1 million gain in Adjusted EBITDA and partly tax paid in 2026 for an underpayment in 2025, and maintenance capital spending rose USD 25.5 million. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending, which management can slow, but about USD 535 million is still to be spent on projects already under construction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is comfortable on every basis available. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 10.55x in FY2025 and income-statement interest 12.23x over the last twelve months. On guided cash interest of USD 115 million to USD 125 million and guided Adjusted EBITDA, cover would be 11.16x to 12.30x, although the issuer's cash interest measure ran USD 19.5 million below the cash paid in the annual report for 2025, so the cash-basis ratio could be lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Referral and partner dependence concentrate operating risk that the filings do not size. About 92% of patients come from acute-care hospitals, which also run competing rehabilitation units, and 37.85% of hospitals are joint ventures whose partners received USD 141.8 million in nine months, 14.81% of operating cash flow, and hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million. A partner's distress or exit would hit volume and could call cash, in an amount that is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10, 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sector structure supports pricing, but its protective barriers are thinning at the edges. The industry outside the company is highly fragmented, patients aged 75 and over are expected to grow about 4% a year through 2030, and about 36% of licensed beds sit in states with certificate-of-need laws, but North Carolina repealed its certificate-of-need requirement for certain providers in July 2026. The annual Medicare update fell from 2.6% for fiscal 2026 to 2.3% for fiscal 2027, and a reform that paid all post-acute care under one system would, on an advisory-body estimate the company cannot verify, cut inpatient rehabilitation payments by 15%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant and legal protection cannot be established, so none is relied on here. The credit agreement sets a maximum leverage ratio of 4.50x and a minimum interest coverage of 3.0x and the company states compliance, but the ratios achieved, the adjustments in their definitions and the executed agreements are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a sound reading is the pairing of rising shareholder returns with wider claim review. Returns have begun to exceed cash after growth spending, total debt rose USD 108.3 million in nine months, lender limits on restricted payments were relaxed in March 2026 and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains; at the same time review reaches about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, no Alabama hospital reached the opt-out rate in the second or third review cycle, and a Q3 bad-debt reserve of 2.7% of revenue shows how quickly collection can slip. The strongest evidence in favour is the company's own room to respond: growth capital spending guided at USD 695 million to USD 755 million is 6.26x to 6.80x the USD 111.1 million fall in Adjusted EBITDA that would take it back to its FY2025 level, where total debt would be 2.05x Adjusted EBITDA, and management guides Q4 bad-debt reserves back to 2.0% to 2.5% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 31, 35, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken if the bad-debt reserve stayed above 2.7% of revenue after the effect of the Q2 system conversion fades, if the revolver were drawn to fund repurchases, or if total debt over Adjusted EBITDA rose above its FY2024 level of 2.26x. It would improve if debt were repaid from free cash flow while earnings keep growing, or if the executed credit agreement and indentures showed wide room under the leverage and restricted-payment tests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, market price or peer was supplied, so the comparison of this business with typical leveraged-credit issuers and any relative-value view are not established, and the sound-credit conclusion rests on the issuer's own history and filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Review outcomes are given only in words for the Alabama hospitals, with no validation rates, denial amounts or payment timing, so the sensitivity to a payment delay of 10 days is an illustration and not a forecast, and the claim-review risk to cash flow could be larger or smaller than shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No independent forecast was run, so the conclusion that earnings keep growing and leverage keeps falling reads management's 2026 guidance and not a tested projection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings-fall scenario is anchored to the FY2025 level of Adjusted EBITDA and not to any covenant test, so it says nothing about how far earnings could fall before a covenant test bound, and no covenant headroom is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer's guided cash interest is USD 19.5 million below the cash interest paid reported for 2025 for reasons the filings do not give, so the cash-basis interest-cover conclusion could be somewhat lower than the ratios shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is earnings growth that lowers leverage without repayment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% in Q3 and total debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.26x at 2024-12-31 to 1.88x at 2026-09-30, because extra revenue earned an incremental margin of 27.58% against an average margin of 21.23%; this widens the gap between cash flow and debt service and supports a low probability of distress while volumes keep growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is a long liquidity and maturity runway. Liquidity of USD 947.6 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 871.4 million to 2031 cover the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities 2.00x, so refinancing risk is remote until 2028 and any slower earnings would be absorbed before creditors are affected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 40; calculation C2; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is non-discretionary, rule-priced demand that is still growing. Discharges rose 5.7% in Q3 and the Medicare rate update of 2.3% from 2026-10-01 sets price in advance, with an ageing population adding about 4% a year to the 75-and-over group, which gives revenue visibility that supports debt service through a normal cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is discretionary growth spending. Growth projects were 73.10% of nine-month capital spending and the 2026 growth plan of USD 695 million to USD 755 million is more than six times the USD 111.1 million fall in earnings used in the downside, so management can protect liquidity in a downturn by slowing expansion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is owned real estate against an unsecured bond structure. The company owns the building at 79.19% of its hospitals and only the revolver is stated to be secured, so a large asset base sits outside the secured claim, although its value and the recovery it would support are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is payer concentration under widening review. Medicare and Medicare Advantage paid 81.8% of revenue and review will cover about 63% of Medicare claims from 2027-01-01, up from about 11.9%, so a delay or denial pushes cash collection back before any change in demand, a mechanism already visible in a bad-debt reserve of 2.7% of Q3 revenue and in Alabama, where no hospital reached the opt-out rate in two cycles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; calculation C4; calculation C15; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is capital allocation that outruns cash flow. Shareholder returns exceeded the cash left after capital spending and partner distributions by USD 62.9 million while debt rose USD 108.3 million, and about USD 955 million of repurchase authorization remains, so leverage can stop falling by choice and debt holders carry that policy risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 44; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is labour cost that is outrunning the Medicare price. Salaries and benefits are 51.72% of revenue and guided to rise 3.5% to 4.0% per employee against a 2.3% Medicare update, so margins depend on staffing productivity that has to keep improving to hold the 21.77% nine-month margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 30; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is a concentrated bond wall at a higher cost. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities are 68.51% of face value and new 2034 debt carries a coupon 137.5 bp above the 2028 notes, so refinancing depends on market access in those years and will probably cost more interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; calculation C2; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is dependence on referral sources and joint-venture partners. About 92% of patients are referred by acute-care hospitals that also run competing units, and partners took USD 141.8 million of distributions in nine months while holding put rights on terms that are not disclosed, so volume and cash calls can change without any change in policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health owns and operates inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico, 67 of them joint ventures with health systems, and reports one segment, so the credit rests on a single service line paid mostly by one federal payer. Revenue of USD 6,338.1 million over the last twelve months is inpatient discharges multiplied by a net price per discharge: in the nine months discharges rose 5.20% and price 3.89%, and new hospitals supplied 2.9 percentage points of the 5.2% discharge growth, so about half of volume growth needs capital before it earns. The model supports cash-flow visibility because payment is set by rule in advance and the conditions treated are not deferred, but it weakens liquidity preservation whenever growth capital is committed ahead of earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 34, 36; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cyclicality is low and concentration is high. Medicare and Medicare Advantage together paid 81.8% of nine-month revenue, 92% of patients arrive from acute-care hospitals and Florida and Texas hold 31.21% of hospitals, so a payment rule, a referral change or a regional disruption each reaches a large share of cash flow at once. Cash generation is real, with operating cash flow of USD 1,303.7 million over the last twelve months, but 73.10% of nine-month capital spending is growth, so the cash left for debt reduction depends on management's choices more than on the business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so sponsor-extraction risks are absent, but the beneficial-ownership table sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied and concentration of holdings is not established. Subsidiary guarantors guarantee the credit agreement, which is secured by personal property, and give full and unconditional senior unsecured guarantees of the notes, while non-guarantor subsidiaries are not summarised separately, so the claims that rank ahead of the notes at those subsidiaries cannot be measured. Joint-venture partners hold noncontrolling interests of USD 821.4 million plus redeemable interests of USD 58.6 million, and their share of income equals 13.66% of nine-month reported EBITDA, so that part of group earnings does not reach the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 8, 18, 44, 45; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the creditor-relevant behaviour. The company reports leverage on its own Adjusted EBITDA and no leverage target appears in the sources. The quarterly dividend rose to USD 0.21 per share in July 2026, repurchases reached USD 203.7 million in nine months and the board raised the authorization to USD 1.0 billion, with about USD 955 million remaining. Growth comes from new hospitals and no acquisition is described or pending, so event risk from large deals is low, but shareholder returns now exceed the cash left after growth, which is why sponsor and governance risk is rated Medium and why creditor alignment is partial.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 43, 44; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume is the stronger driver and price is set mostly by rule. Discharges rose 5.7% in Q3, 3.0% same-store and 2.7% from new hospitals, and Q3 occupancy of 77.0% leaves room to fill existing beds, which is cheaper growth than building. The Medicare update is 2.3% from 2026-10-01 after 2.6% a year earlier, managed care pricing is guided at 3.5% to 4.0% and Medicaid is only 3.0% of revenue, so pricing power is weakest with the largest payer and better only where contracts are negotiated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7, 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 33, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable, regulated and concentrated, not cyclical or structurally declining, because rehabilitation admissions follow stroke, brain injury and hip fracture that are not deferred. It is exposed to substitution at the margin, since nursing homes may market rehabilitation to patients who do not need intensive therapy, and to reform of post-acute payment. Medicare fee-for-service rose to 66.3% of Q3 revenue from 64.1% while Medicare Advantage fell to 15.7% from 16.6%, and claim review applies only to fee-for-service claims, so the mix shift raises exposure at the moment the review widens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labour is the main cost and it flexes partly with occupied beds. Salaries and benefits were 52.2% of Q3 revenue against 53.1% a year earlier, employees per occupied bed were 3.38 against 3.42 and contract labour fell 23.2%, which is how margin was held while pay per employee rose. Because Medicare pays a fixed amount per discharge and the hospital keeps the difference from its cost, every saving or overrun is a margin change, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.53% in Q3 against 20.31%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C5; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin is easier to defend against slower volume than against wage inflation. The incremental margin of 27.58% shows operating leverage that cuts both ways, so slower volume would reduce earnings faster than revenue. Pay per employee is guided up 3.5% to 4.0% against a 2.3% Medicare update, a gap of 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points on 65.7% of revenue, and pre-opening and ramp-up costs of USD 15.8 million in nine months, guided at USD 20 million to USD 24 million for the year, weigh on margin while new hospitals fill. Downside cost flexibility sits mostly in staffing and hiring, because occupancy costs are only 0.9% of Q3 revenue on largely owned buildings and depreciation is already 5.9%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 34; calculation C5; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and mostly chosen. Capital spending was 12.88% of nine-month revenue, of which USD 166.0 million, 26.90%, was maintenance and USD 451.2 million, 73.10%, was growth; the 2026 plan is USD 920 million to USD 995 million with USD 225 million to USD 240 million of maintenance, and about USD 535 million more is needed to finish projects under construction. On the issuer's measure 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA converts to free cash flow before growth capital and shareholder returns, so cash for debt reduction is what remains after management decides how much growth to fund.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other claims on cash sit beside the debt figure. Finance leases of USD 274.9 million are inside it, while operating lease liabilities of USD 204.3 million, purchase obligations of USD 197.4 million and future interest of USD 544.5 million on debt other than finance leases are outside it. Cash interest is guided at USD 115 million to USD 125 million and cash taxes at USD 200 million to USD 220 million for 2026, so fixed charges are covered many times by Adjusted EBITDA, and the ability to slow growth spending is the main protection if earnings fall before the 2028 to 2031 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is local and moderate. The industry outside the company is fragmented and the main competitors are rehabilitation units inside acute-care hospitals, which can be formidable where a large system dominates the local market, and one public company that mainly provides other post-acute care also runs 38 rehabilitation hospitals. Because 92% of patients are referred by acute-care hospitals, a system that opens its own unit can divert referrals, a volume risk market by market and not a pricing risk, since Medicare sets the price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New entry is limited by capital and regulation but the limit is eroding at the edges. Certificate-of-need laws cover about 36% of licensed beds, yet North Carolina repealed its requirement for certain providers in July 2026 and the company accelerated the amortization of its asset there by USD 2.9 million. Entry still needs hospital-scale capital and Medicare qualification, including the rule that a set share of admissions must come from listed medical conditions, so it is slow, but where approval is no longer needed a rival's new beds would compete for the company's referral sources directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes pull at the margin. Nursing homes may market rehabilitation to patients who do not need intensive therapy, and a bundled-payment programme that covers 2% of the company's discharges, with 89 of its hospitals in the affected markets, gives acute-care hospitals a financial reason to choose the cheapest setting, although they may not restrict a patient's choice. The effect is on lower-acuity volume and is small today, and it would matter to creditors only if bundled payment widened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high in structure and low in practice. Medicare pays 65.7% of revenue and sets price by rule, while Medicare Advantage at 16.1% and managed care at 10.7% are negotiated under contracts that typically run one to three years, with typical rate increases of 2% to 4% in 2025, and acute-care referral sources are the gatekeepers. The company cannot negotiate with its largest payer, so rate rules and review programmes pass straight into margin and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power sits mainly in clinical labour. Salaries and benefits are 51.72% of revenue and guided to rise 3.5% to 4.0% per employee, whereas supplies were 4.0% of Q3 revenue against 4.4%, so wage competition rather than input cost is what can compress margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only three categories change the credit view. Regulatory policy is the largest, because the annual payment rule, the review demonstration and any move to a single post-acute payment system act directly on price and cash collection. Social change supports demand, since the population aged 75 and over is expected to grow about 4% a year through 2030 and the average Medicare patient is about 77. Technology mattered in 2026: a billing and collecting disruption after a system conversion pushed bad-debt reserves to 2.7% of Q3 revenue from 1.9%, a direct cash effect of an operating change, which management expects to ease to 2.0% to 2.5% in Q4.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic factors and currency are not a primary driver of credit quality. The company operates in the United States and Puerto Rico, wage inflation is dealt with under cost, and the only reference to tariffs is a general risk statement with no stated effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-supportive factors are earnings growth that is lowering leverage, liquidity of USD 947.6 million with a revolver to 2031 that covers the 2028 maturities 2.00x, rule-priced non-discretionary demand and growth capital that management can slow. The credit constraints are payer concentration under widening review, capital allocation that has outrun cash flow, pay growth above the Medicare update and a bond wall of 68.51% of face value in 2028, 2030 and 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C2; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only some opportunities could improve credit quality. Q3 occupancy of 77.0% leaves room to fill existing beds; planned additions of 4.66% to 5.05% of licensed beds in 2026 add capacity; revenue growth has so far carried an incremental margin above the average; and repayment of the revolver from free cash flow would raise protection further. The threats are review extended beyond the announced hospitals, a move to one post-acute payment system that an advisory body estimated would cut payments by 15%, and loss of a joint-venture partner or referral relationship.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C5; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine dimensions are assessed as Strong, Average or Weak, each with the evidence behind it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and market position is Strong: revenue of USD 6,338.1 million over the last twelve months, Q3 occupancy of 77.0% and the company's own description as the largest owner and operator give the scale to absorb a regional shock, although no market-share data were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Competitive advantage is Average: certificate-of-need laws protect only about 36% of licensed beds and one state repealed its requirement for certain providers, and the clinical-outcome advantage is a management statement, so the moat does not offset the payment-rule risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business diversification is Weak: one segment, 81.8% of revenue from Medicare and Medicare Advantage, 92% of patients from acute-care hospitals and 31.21% of hospitals in Florida and Texas leave no offset to a rule change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 110; calculation C4; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility is Average: 73.10% of capital spending is growth and can be slowed, but about USD 535 million is committed to projects under construction and labour is 51.72% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C10; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin stability is Average: the nine-month margin rose to 21.77%, but pay growth exceeds the Medicare update by 1.2 percentage points to 1.7 percentage points and the incremental margin cuts both ways.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow stability is Average: free cash flow before distributions was USD 457.2 million over the last twelve months and conversion on the issuer's measure is 60.78%, but taxes and growth capital absorb it and the nine months ended with a shortfall after shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average: USD 600 million of 2034 notes were sold in 2026, USD 500 million at par and USD 100 million at 98.75%, which shows access, but the new coupon is 137.5 bp higher than the 2028 notes and no rating or market price was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity position is Strong: liquidity of USD 947.6 million is 0.36x total debt, the revolver runs to 2031-03-09 and scheduled principal through 2027 is only USD 56.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance is Average: no sponsor and falling leverage weigh against shareholder returns above free cash flow and a Medium governance rating, with covenant detail and board information not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are earnings growth, liquidity and a distant first maturity, and the main constraints are single-payer concentration, capital allocation and pay growth. Leverage on Adjusted EBITDA has improved from 2.26x to 1.88x while conversion has eased from 64.51% to 60.78%, so the trend is better on balance sheet and flat to weaker on cash. The key missing datapoints are the covenant ratios achieved, claim-review outcomes, ratings, the proxy statement and the executed debt agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months management guides 2026 revenue of USD 6,450 million to USD 6,500 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,395 million to USD 1,415 million, raised from USD 1,365 million to USD 1,395 million, with eight new hospitals and further bed additions in 2026 and a similar programme planned for 2027. The tailwinds are the 2.3% Medicare update from 2026-10-01 and managed care pricing of 3.5% to 4.0%, which support revenue and margin. The headwinds are claim review from 2027-01-01, pay growth of 3.5% to 4.0% per employee and a bad-debt reserve guided at 2.0% to 2.5% of Q4 revenue, which press on margin and cash flow. Guided free cash flow of USD 770 million to USD 865 million and a growth plan of USD 695 million to USD 755 million leave leverage falling only if earnings grow, because debt reduction and repurchases are both unset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 31; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years management targets 6 to 10 new hospitals a year and discharge growth of 6% to 8% through 2027, and the population aged 75 and over is expected to grow about 4% a year to 2030, a tailwind to volume that supports deleveraging if capital spending is paced. The bundled-payment programme runs to December 2030 and a single post-acute payment system, if adopted, would on an advisory-body estimate cut payments by 15%, both headwinds to price. The 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities fall in this window, so market access at that time, not performance now, sets refinancing cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 46; calculation C16; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario that fits this issuer is payment friction meeting pay growth. From 2027-01-01 about 63% of Medicare claims, up from about 11.9%, go through pre-claim or post-payment review, while the Medicare rate rises 2.3% and pay per employee 3.5% to 4.0%. In Alabama, the first state reviewed, no company hospital reached the opt-out validation rate in the second or third cycle, so full pre-claim review stayed in force there. The first break is in collections: review lengthens the time to payment and lifts denials, bad-debt reserves stay at the 2.7% of revenue seen in Q3 instead of easing to the guided 2.0% to 2.5%, and the receivables build of USD 89.5 million in nine months repeats.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 31, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_ehc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is delayed before it is lost, so cash falls before earnings. Holding the reserve 80 bp above its year-earlier level costs USD 12.88 million a quarter, 3.71% of Q3 Adjusted EBITDA, and each 10 days of added delay on the Medicare revenue under review ties up about USD 67.0 million. A delay of 30 days, with Adjusted EBITDA also falling back by USD 111.1 million to its FY2025 level, would absorb USD 312.1 million, which is 32.94% of liquidity of USD 947.6 million, and total debt would be 2.05x Adjusted EBITDA against 1.88x. The length of delay is an assumption for illustration, because the filings print no payment timing for reviewed claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 35; calculation C1; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers well above that size. Growth capital spending is guided at USD 695 million to USD 755 million, repurchases were USD 203.7 million in nine months and dividends are about USD 79 million for 2026, so liquidity distress is avoided if growth and repurchases are slowed when collections weaken. The scenario fails only if repurchases and the committed projects of about USD 535 million continue while collections are delayed and the revolver funds the gap, which would raise secured debt ahead of the notes and shorten the runway to the USD 436.0 million of 2028 maturities. We do not assume default: the evidence shows enough resilience to avoid distress with an ordinary management response, but covenant headroom is not established, so the point at which the tests bind is unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 17, 43; calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Encompass Health presents an adequate business profile supported by owned scale in a rule-priced, non-discretionary service and an earnings base that is growing, but credit quality is constrained by payer concentration under widening claim review, capital allocation that has outrun cash flow and pay growth above the Medicare update. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because issuer-defined free cash flow converts 60.78% of Adjusted EBITDA before growth capital, although taxes and growth spending are lowering the share. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for the 2028, 2030 and 2031 maturities, which are 68.51% of face value, backed by liquidity of USD 947.6 million and a revolver to 2031. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer or rating data were supplied. The primary downside path is slower Medicare collection under wider review combined with pay growth above the rate update while repurchases continue. Further analysis would require the covenant ratios achieved, the executed credit agreement and indentures, claim-review outcome data, ratings, peer data and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ehc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 31, 40; EX-99.2_2026-10-28_ehcq32026earningsslides_.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: Medicare payment policy and claim review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. The seven filings and presentations cover FY2025 and each 2026 quarter to 2026-09-30 and support every step. Ratings, market prices, peers, the proxy statement and the executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, which limits the peer comparison, governance depth and covenant conclusions. The figures taken from the earlier modules were used as stated and, where a page is cited beside them, agree with it, except that Financial foundation lists the 2024 hospital count as absent from the sources while the annual report prints it, as Business & governance states; the count is not used in any conclusion here.
